paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and oxidation resistance of Fe-Al-Nb alloyed layer on 45 steel by plasma surface modification

evidence.section: Title
evidence.quote: The Fe-Al-Nb alloyed layer was coated on 45 steel by the plasma niobiumizing modification to improve the microstructure and oxidation resistance of Fe-Al coating prepared by hot-dipping aluminum.

evidence.section: 2.1 Specimen preparation
evidence.quote: The 45 steel was employed as the substrate, which was cut into square shape with the dimension of 15 mm × 15 mm × 3 mm.

evidence.section: 2.1 Specimen preparation
evidence.quote: The specimens were immersed in pure aluminum melt at 1023 K for 120 s, pulled out slowly at a constant speed and then air-cooled to room temperature.

evidence.section: 2.1 Specimen preparation
evidence.quote: After hot-dipping, the aluminized samples were diffusion annealing treated in a tube furnace with the protection of Ar atmosphere at 1223 K for 4 h, and then cooled along with the furnace to room temperature.

evidence.section: 2.1 Specimen preparation
evidence.quote: The plasma surface modification technology was operated in a vacuum chamber to prepare Fe-Al-Nb alloyed layer on the Fe-Al coating. The source electrode is pure Nb target (Φ100 × 3 mm), the other electrode is hot-dipping sample. Initially, the chamber was evacuated to less than 3.0 Pa and then filled with Ar to 40 Pa, the sequence was repeated two or three times. The substrate and the source electrode were all connected to direct current power; the distance between them was 20 mm. While the equipment was on steady state, source and substrate electrode voltage were 850 V and 400 V, respectively. The Nb atoms diffused into the substrate at temperature of approximately 1073 K.

evidence.quote: the alloyed layer displays a couple of phases, including Fe3Al, FeAl, Fe2Nb (i.e. Laves phase) and Nb carbides (i.e. NbC and Nb6C5)

evidence.section: 3.2 Isothermal oxidation test of the alloyed layer
evidence.quote: there is a continuous layer of alumina (i.e. internal oxidation) between the loose iron oxides layer and the uniform Fe-Al-Nb alloyed layer, protecting the internal coating from further effects of oxygen.
